Navi Pillay’s Nobel Peace Prize: ICJ and ICC Explained

On October ninth, twenty twenty-six, the Norwegian Nobel Committee announced South African jurist Navi Pillay as the Nobel Peace Prize laureate. The committee credited her work promoting peace and international law. Two courts help explain the legal landscape. The International Court of Justice handles disputes between states that accept its jurisdiction and gives advisory opinions requested by authorized United Nations bodies. The International Criminal Court investigates and, where warranted within its jurisdiction, tries individuals accused of specified international crimes. It complements national courts. When reading coverage, check the court, the parties and the procedural stage. An award or inquiry report is not a final criminal conviction.
